chapter: Kid Rene, Chris Kelly and the bungalow
title: What made Chris Kelly's band stand out on the blues
summary: Kelly played plunger-muted trumpet on Kelly's Love and the band had no printed arrangements.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Was there anything that made the Chris Kelly band stand out so on the blues? What made you so good on the blues?

Well, we had a blues down there used to call it Keller's Love. And he was the only man that could play the Keller's Love. I mean, to suit the people, the puck. Because he used to use that wah-wah on his trumpet. And he used to say he was talking. Oh yeah. Did he use his hand or a plunger, a rubber plunger? A plunger. Rubber plunger. He was a good blues man. Did he sound anything like Joe Oliver on the blues, would you say? Did Oliver use much of that newt work too? Yeah, yeah. He was good. He was the blues king down there. He had more so a blues band than anything else.
Well, you wouldn't say that he played a lot of fast notes or anything like that? Or did he mix it up? Well, he'd mix it up. He could make fast drums or slow stuff. Yeah. Whatever suited, I guess.
Did the Chris Kelly band ever use any arrangements, the printed music, any stock arrangements? Or anything? No, no, no. Just everything in their head? Anything in their head.
That's all. Did they ever play any of those members you were saying that Buddy Petit played like Scott Joplin?
